independence_declaration.statement:
I am code-security-reviewer, session da744e37-29eb-4508-aad0-60d57fdbc700, task T-DG7-REV-CS-RG2. I verified the assignment's SHA-256 (3490c28cadf73a8cfb3bdcb31b4251d015aa7cd19c5ce99fc0d93428c29eac7c).

I authored no implementation in the DG7 scope. P7 and its repairs (DO-D11 by devops-engineer, SA-ADR71 by solution-architect) were built by implementer roles. qa-verifier wrote the pre-freeze acceptance tests, and delivery-orchestrator integrated the work and ran the drills.

I formed this verdict without opening any other reviewer's round-2 record or evidence; I read only my own role's round-1 findings, to verify them. HEAD at the start was 1c119c031. The commits after source_commit 152db5b51 (c26f69d70, 1c119c031) touch only the three assignments, the frozen manifest and stages.json.

Two inconsistencies in the assignment are reported, not followed:
- It asks for `round: 7`, but the record path is round-2, and tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs l.682/794 requires rec.round to equal the round directory and the stages.json round entry. This record says round 2.
- It names docs/delivery/reviews/DG5/round-7/code-security-reviewer.json as the field-set template, but DG5 has no round 7 (rounds 1-5 only). I mirrored the field set of docs/delivery/reviews/DG7/round-1/code-security-reviewer.json, which is the schema's full property set.

This review is engineering evidence only. It grants no business, Finance or IT approval. Product gate G6 does not imply DG7, and DG7 implies no G1-G6 approval.

checks_run.expected: candidate sha256:33266ccd9ce4ec4475de745ebacfaafbd2f25870f8be966086f4a74578b7259c over 3158 files; the commits after the source commit change only metadata.
checks_run.actual:
HEAD is 1c119c031. The diff 152db5b51..HEAD touches only the three round-2 assignments, candidates/DG7/33266ccd9ce4ec44.manifest.json and stages.json, all excluded from the candidate.

candidate.mjs gives sha256:33266ccd9ce4ec4475de745ebacfaafbd2f25870f8be966086f4a74578b7259c over 3158 files, exit 0. --diff gives matches: true, with added, removed and changed all empty.

checks_run.procedure: Re-run the round-1 S3 reproduction on this candidate's scanner, extended with probes of the remaining exemptions. Values are generated at run time under $TMPDIR with openssl, and none is committed.
checks_run.environment: Disposable sparse clone at 152db5b51; Node v24.21.0; OpenSSL.
checks_run.expected: Round-1 cases (a) 48-hex POSTGRES_PASSWORD and (c) 24 lower-case OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET are reported S3 with exit 1, like the (d) mixed-case control. A real i18n key (i) stays exempt.
checks_run.actual:
(a), (c) and (d) each give one S3 hit, 'secret-scan: FAIL (1 hits)', exit 1, and the value is masked. In round 1, (a) and (c) gave PASS, exit 0. (i) 'auth.password.reset_hint_text' gives PASS, exit 0.

The exit-0 results in this log, each explained:
- (b) 32-hex: this draw's entropy is 3.44, below the ADR-0063 threshold of 3.5, so it is not reported. isI18nKey is false, so this is not the i18n defect; SEC-RG2-11 measures the rate.
- (e) 64-hex secret_access_key: the checksum exemption, disclosed in SC-13; see F-DG7-1041.
- (f) upper-case hex: this draw's entropy is 3.06, below the threshold.
- (g) base32 upper-case: the 'key NAME' rule.
- (h) four lower-case words joined by '_': the i18n-key shape, inherently indistinguishable from a passphrase (ADR-0063 §5 residual 1).
(e) to (h) are probes of other rules, not the round-1 defect. The script itself exits 0.

checks_run.procedure: Measure how many random generated secrets per shape the S3 rule does not report, and why: entropy, i18n key, or key NAME (5000 samples each). Then run a probe scanner without the 64-hex and key-NAME exemptions over the payload, to see whether any real value hides behind them today.
checks_run.command: node docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG7/code-security/round-2/repro/s3-exemption-rates.mjs $TMPDIR/review-cs 5000; node tools/release/secret-scan-probe.mjs --scope payload (disposable copy in the clone; diff in 12-secret-scan-probe.diff); the same probe with --path over the 7 docs/delivery manifest entries
checks_run.environment: Disposable sparse clone at 152db5b51 (the probe file was deleted afterwards); Node v24.21.0.
checks_run.expected: isI18nKey exempts no generated secret. The remaining non-reports are explained by documented rules. The probe's extra hits, if any, are not secrets.

checks_run.procedure: Re-run the round-1 backup-mode probe on a disposable PostgreSQL: backup.sh --phase database under umask 022 with MTH_TRANSFER_ATTACHMENTS=none, the Compose service's sequence. Also probe the new root checks: a 1777 root, a symlinked root, and a foreign-owned 0700 root.
checks_run.command: QA_PG_PORT=32460 MTH_PORT_POOL=32400-32499 LANG= LC_ALL= tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh bash docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG7/code-security/round-2/repro/backup-set-mode-rg2.sh $TMPDIR/review-cs
checks_run.environment: Disposable sparse clone at 152db5b51; disposable PostgreSQL 16.15 on port 32460; migrations 0001-0152 (135 applied); sandbox uid 0 with umask set to 022.
checks_run.expected: Every set entry is 0700 or 0600, with nothing open to group or others. A 1777 root is refused with exit 2 and nothing written.
checks_run.actual:
P1: backup.sh exit 0. The root, the set, .backup-state/*, config/*, db/database.dump and db/table-counts.tsv are all 700 (d) or 600 (f), and no entry has a group or other bit. In round 1 they were 755/644. The dump holds TABLE DATA app_user, audit_event and session.

P2: the 1777 root gives 'BLOCKED: the backup root <W>/shared is writable by group or others; use an owner-only directory (chmod 0700)', exit 2, 0 entries written.

P3 (observation): a symlinked root to a 0700 directory is refused with exit 2 and the same 'writable by group or others' text. The refusal is fail-closed, but the message is misleading, because find -perm reads the symlink's own mode (0777). In Compose the bind mount resolves symlinks, so /backups is the directory itself.

P4: BLOCKED in this sandbox (chown to 65534 is not permitted). Statically, backup.sh checks the root's mode, not its owner. Hardening observation: a 0700 root pre-created by another account would be accepted. That needs the operator to point MTH_BACKUP_ROOT at another account's directory, while backup-restore.md §3.2 creates it with install -d -m 0700 -o root -g root and the /tmp default is gone.

The probe script exits 0, and so does the harness. The 'BLOCKED' and 'exit=2' lines are the asserted refusals, explained above.

checks_run.procedure: Judge the D-282 widening of the finding-id pattern. Read every place in the gate tooling that parses or orders finding ids.
checks_run.command: git diff ddf42ccd2..152db5b51 -- tools/gates/schemas/findings.schema.json; grep -rnE 'F-DG|\[0-9\]\{3\}' tools/gates/*.mjs tools/gates/lib/*.mjs; read tools/gates/import-findings.mjs l.40-75, tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs l.486-570

checks_run.actual: Only the pattern changed: ^F-DG[0-7]-[0-9]{3}$ became ^F-DG[0-7]-[0-9]{3,4}$. Ownership and relabel checks use the prefix `F-${stage}-` (import-findings.mjs l.48; rules.mjs l.491, 553, 556), so F-DG7-1041 still belongs only to DG7. No tool assumes a fixed length or sorts ids lexically for closure. Closure is keyed by the exact id (collectVerifications). Every existing 3-digit id stays valid. The change is sound.

checks_run.command: QA_PG_PORT=32480 MTH_PORT_POOL=32400-32499 LANG= LC_ALL= tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project integration apps/api/test/integration/transfer apps/api/test/integration/retention apps/api/test/integration/release apps/api/test/integration/identity/unbound-signin.test.ts apps/api/test/integration/aud-write-deny.test.ts apps/api/test/integration/platform/deployment-status.test.ts apps/api/test/integration/platform/readiness-storage-worker.test.ts apps/worker/test/integration/retention-archive.test.ts packages/db/test/integration/p7-retention-guards.test.ts packages/db/test/integration/p7-transfer-guards.test.ts packages/db/test/integration/transfer-roundtrip.test.ts packages/db/test/integration/transfer-load.test.ts packages/db/test/integration/transfer-export.test.ts packages/db/test/integration/transfer-locks.test.ts; then the failing file alone, 3 times (port 32490)
checks_run.environment: Disposable sparse clone at 152db5b51 with the repository's read-only node_modules symlinked; disposable PostgreSQL 16.15; Vitest 3.2.7. The P7 unit run (SEC-RG2-41) ran concurrently.
checks_run.expected: All tests pass, with no unexplained failure.
checks_run.actual:
322/322 tests pass, but Vitest reports '1 failed | 21 passed (22)' test files, exit 1. The failed 'suite' is the afterAll teardown of packages/db/test/integration/p7-transfer-guards.test.ts: 'test teardown: 1 connection(s) to mth_p7guard_... are still open, so it is not dropped (a pool or client was not ended): ? (active)', thrown by dropScratchDatabase in packages/db/test/global-setup.ts l.144 after its 10 s grace period.

Explanation: the test's own pools carry application names (test-app-p7guard, test-owner-p7guard), and both are destroyed first. The leftover backend had no application name and was 'active'. otherBackends() (global-setup.ts l.110-115) counts every backend on the database without filtering backend_type. The most likely cause is an autovacuum worker on the freshly loaded scratch database outliving the 10 s window under load: the unit run was sharing the CPU. I could not prove that, because the backend was gone by the time I looked.

The file re-run alone three times gives 22/22, exit 0, each time (30b-...-1/2/3). The orchestrator's full pre-freeze integration run passed it too (475/475 files). This is a DG1-era test-harness sensitivity, not a product defect, and no assertion failed.

It is a timeout, not an assertion failure. The test parses the 965-operation OpenAPI contract while the integration suite was loading the CPU.

Re-run alone: 3/3 pass, exit 0. The same test takes 3289 ms against the 5000 ms limit, so it is load-sensitive. The orchestrator's pre-freeze unit run passed it (3042/3042).

checks_run.procedure: Direct source review of the security-relevant P7 paths, re-judged on this candidate. Since round 1 (ddf42ccd2..152db5b51), product source changed only in deploy/scripts/backup.sh, deploy/compose/compose.yaml, deploy/service-list.json, tools/release/secret-scan.mjs, findings.schema.json and their tests. Everything else is byte-identical to the round-1 candidate.
checks_run.command: git diff --stat ddf42ccd2630f3d62f6aaf360ff401bbc2bde025..152db5b51 -- . ':!docs/delivery/{runs,reviews,test-evidence,handbacks}'; read apps/api/src/modules/transfer/config-bundle/{routes,service}.ts, packages/db/src/transfer/import.ts, packages/config/src/load.ts l.397-423, apps/api/src/modules/identity/oidc.ts l.60-95, tools/release/secret-scan.mjs, deploy/scripts/backup.sh
checks_run.expected: Every mutation has server-side authorization, validation, optimistic concurrency and an audit event. The audit stays append-only. The loopback exception is exact. The new shell code is safe.
checks_run.actual:
Config-bundle routes: every operation does requireSomeRight plus an organization-scoped requireRightAt, with strict zod params and query. Upload has a 5 MiB declared and streamed limit (413). Commit runs in one transaction: freshRightAt (grants reloaded in the transaction), lockedImport (If-Match version), a re-plan compared with the stored validation (planChanged rolls back), each kind's adapter enforcing its own configure right, an UPDATE ... WHERE version, and an audit event config_bundle_import.committed.

Observation: GET by id returns 404 for a missing id and 403 for another organization's id, an existence oracle limited to UUIDv7 ids. This is the project-wide convention, not new.

Migration import: LOCK TABLE audit_event IN EXCLUSIVE MODE; both immutability triggers are checked enabled ('O'); user triggers are disabled only on the other tables; audit_event is never updated, deleted or truncated, and a deferred audit column is refused (D-258).

OIDC loopback: secureIssuerAllowed allows http only for the hostnames localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1], after WHATWG normalisation, and only in production. allowInsecureRequests is set only for that case.

Hardening observation: allowInsecureRequests applies to every endpoint the loopback issuer's discovery returns, so an operator-controlled local drill IdP that advertised a remote http token endpoint would be followed. That is bounded to the D-258 drill configuration and is not reachable by an outside party.

backup.sh: umask 077 is scoped to backup_main, so restore.sh keeps its own; chmod -R does not follow symlinks met during traversal; the ownerOnly check fails the set.

Round-1 findings F-DG7-1001 and F-DG7-1022 (records): I agree with D-282's disclosure; neither has a product effect. The asset-scan allow-list, Dockerfile, image bundle and seal/verify tools are unchanged since round 1.

checks.log: 19 checks, exit 0. These include typecheck, lint, openapi-lint (965 operations), prettier, pnpm test (unit-node 3042/3042, unit-web 2199/2199, formula-nocodegen 259 + 2 skipped), and test:integration (475 files; 4696 pass, 8 skipped, 1 todo). They also include transfer-drill 70/70, release-tool 479 (477 pass, 2 skipped, 0 fail), deploy tools 125/125, e2e-retention, the secret payload and history scans, the claims scan and historical DG6.

The skips and failures:
- The two release-tool skips are T-A11, marked BLOCKED (no assembled runtime tree; the real-build asset scan is the orchestrator's host evidence), and T-A3 (bsdtar not installed).
- The 'fail' and 'error' greps in the logs are test names (fixtures that assert failure), not failures.

Of the hits, 33 are DG7: 24 assignments lacking task/requirement ids or other elements, 7 handbacks lacking one section, the a0fbc6f1 assignment-hash mismatch (F-DG7-1001, D-282), and one historical-evidence timing hit. All are process records disclosed under D-249/D-270/D-282 in known-limitations.md. None comes from DO-D11 or SA-ADR71, and none affects product behaviour.

Live CI was not run (D-058). That is environmental, recorded as PASS on the offline surface.

checks_run.command: grep '^| D-2(49|67|69|70|74|78|80|81|82) ' docs/delivery/decisions.md; read docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0065-*.md Amendment 1; packages/shared/src/transfer/config-bundle.ts l.30-60; ls docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG7/orchestrator/host/

summary: PASS on sha256:33266ccd. All three round-1 findings I reported are CLOSED_VERIFIED on this candidate. F-DG7-1011: the narrowed i18n rule exempts 0% of generated secrets, and the scans add no false positive. F-DG7-1012: the set is owner-only, a 1777 root is refused, and the /tmp fallback is gone. F-DG7-1013: ADR-0071 Amendment 1 matches the code. One new Low, non-mandatory finding, F-DG7-1041: ADR-0063 §1.2/§5 and ADR-0066 §4 were not amended for the DO-D11 behaviour. It is documentation drift and does not block. Every failure in my logs is explained: a no-node_modules load error, a load timeout, a teardown connection after 322/322 passing tests, and a masked protocol-audit exit. Each was re-run clean where possible. The D-282 schema widening is sound. Nothing is Critical, High or mandatory. This record grants no business, Finance or IT approval and does not imply DG7.
